generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, this shows up the moment you write about studies. You decide what you want to argue, say about a behaviour or an intervention, then bring findings in to support it and weigh their limits. The structure, the studies and your critical reading of them all serve that one argument.
generatedProse.worked-example: A psychology student writes an essay on whether a therapy works. At first they summarise each study in turn, then note at the end that samples were small. Rewriting, they lead with their argument, bring supporting and contrasting studies in to serve it, and hedge each claim as they go. Now the structure, the studies and their critical reading all carry one argument.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, your argument leads and the studies serve it. You structure the essay to carry one case, integrate findings to support it, and signal your judgements about their strength. Keeping your argument in charge is what turns a review of studies into an argument of your own.

check.body: A student plans one argument, structures the essay so each paragraph moves it forward, leads paragraphs in their own voice with sources, and signals their judgements. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: Argument-led writing at work: structure, sources and a critical edge all serving one argument.
_items.feedback: Yes. The three moves are working together as one practice, with the argument in charge.

_items.text: That the student used too many sources and should cut some out.
_items.feedback: The number of sources is not the point. The point is that they all serve one argument.

_items.text: That structure alone was enough to make the essay strong.
_items.feedback: Structure is one part. Here it works with integrated sources and a critical edge.

_items.text: That the critical edge was added at the end, separate from the rest.
_items.feedback: The critical edge ran through the writing, not tacked on. It is part of one practice.
